exposure: Eliminating routine ordering of oral opioids after cesarean delivery
Implementing guidelines for ordering a short course of opioids when deemed necessary
Coupling opioid prescribing at discharge to patterns of opioid use in-hospital combined with shared decision-making
outcome: Percentage of women who used any opioids postoperatively in-hospital
Percentage of women discharged with a prescription for opioids
Opioid prescriptions ordered in the 6 weeks after delivery
cohort: The study included 191 post-cesarean delivery patients before the intervention and 181 after the intervention at a tertiary care center.
finding: Eliminating routine ordering of oral opioids after cesarean delivery significantly decreased in-hospital opioid consumption (45% vs 68%) and discharge opioid prescriptions (40% vs 91%) without changing pain scores or overall patient satisfaction.
mod_finding: The quality improvement intervention successfully reduced opioid use and prescribing after cesarean delivery.
followup_time: 12 weeks after delivery (for survey outcomes) and 6 weeks after delivery (for prescription outcomes)
